name: POST /api/leadflow/consent/receipts - issue one signed, purpose-specific consent receipt
description:
Issues a consent receipt from the Capture Consent modal (#consentModal): one subject, ONE purpose, the channels agreed for it, the notice they were shown, and the signature evidence.

ONE PURPOSE PER RECEIPT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A RULE WE ENFORCE (AC1). sdk-consent's validateGrantConsent takes a singular `purpose_id`, so a receipt cannot carry two purposes even if a caller wanted it to - blanket consent is impossible by construction rather than by validation. This endpoint mirrors that: `purpose_id` is a single string and an array is rejected. A screen that let an operator tick four purposes and issue one receipt would be issuing a permission nobody granted.

PROMOTIONAL OFFERS IS ITS OWN PURPOSE, NEVER A CHANNEL (AC4). It is the one purpose people most often did not intend to agree to, and bundling it as a checkbox under a service purpose is precisely how that happens: somebody consents to job updates and finds themselves on a marketing list. Sending it as a channel is rejected with a message that says why, rather than being silently dropped - a silent drop leaves the operator believing they captured it.

THE SIGNATURE IS ENCRYPTED BEFORE IT IS STORED, AND IS NOT SEARCHABLE (AC2). The image goes to sdk-vault POST /api/vault/encrypt and only the returned ciphertext reference is kept; the raw data URL is never persisted and never logged. It is deliberately excluded from any contact-search projection - a signature is evidence for a specific dispute, not an attribute of a person to be browsed.

THE NOTICE IS RECORDED AS SHOWN, NOT AS NAMED (AC3). notice_hash, the displayed text, the language, the device and the capturing representative are all required. "Which version did they see" is the first question asked when a consent is challenged, and a template id alone cannot answer it: templates change, and the one on file today may not be the words on the screen that day.

DEGRADES NOWHERE. Every part of this is a WRITE. If the vault cannot encrypt the signature, or sdk-consent cannot record the receipt, this answers an error rather than a partial success - a receipt without its evidence is worse than no receipt, because it looks complete.

requiresRole:["privacy_officer"] and NO testCase pins an Authorization header (MUST-71). QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: NEGATIVE: two purposes on one receipt are refused - no blanket consent

payload.notice_text: We will contact you about your job.

testCases.name: NEGATIVE: promotional offers sent as a channel is refused, not silently dropped

payload.notice_text: We will contact you about your job.

testCases.name: NEGATIVE: a receipt with no notice evidence is refused

errorCases.message: purpose_id must be a single purpose; a receipt covers exactly one
errorCases.when: purpose_id is an array or absent. Mirrors sdk-consent, whose validateGrantConsent takes a singular purpose_id - blanket consent is impossible upstream and must not be constructible here either.

errorCases.message: promotional_offers is a separate purpose, not a channel
errorCases.when: promotional_offers appears in channels. Refused loudly rather than dropped: a silent drop leaves the operator believing they captured a marketing permission they did not.

errorCases.message: notice_hash, notice_text and notice_language are required
errorCases.when: any part of the notice evidence is missing. A template id cannot answer 'which words did they see', because templates change.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the header is absent or not Bearer. Not authored as a testCase: pinning it would defeat the role swap (MUST-71).

errorCases.message: No policy grants this action to the caller's roles.
errorCases.when: the caller does not hold consent.purpose_manage.

errorCases.message: The signature could not be encrypted, so the receipt was not issued.
errorCases.when: sdk-vault or sdk-consent is unreachable. Deliberately NOT a partial success: a receipt without its evidence is worse than no receipt, because it looks complete.
